memories.author: D05
memories.text: Asthma, intermittent. Patient reports occasional wheezing after exertion, no night symptoms. BPH stable on tamsulosin and finasteride, no urinary obstruction. Exam: mild expiratory wheeze bilaterally, normal cardiovascular, prostate not enlarged on DRE. Spirometry: FEV1 2.85 L (92% pred), FVC 3.60 L (95% pred), FEV1/FVC 0.79; change from baseline +0.10 L. ACT score 22 (well controlled). Technique checked: correct with salbutamol MDI. Smoking: never.

memories.text: Refer to Urology for evaluation of benign prostatic hyperplasia. Patient on tamsulosin and finasteride, PSA 1.2, wishes to discuss long‑term management and surgical options if needed.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Asthma, intermittent. Patient notes no wheeze in past month, uses salbutamol <2 times/week. BPH: no change in urinary symptoms, no retention. Exam: clear lungs, normal cardiac, prostate benign on DRE. Spirometry: FEV1 2.90 L (94% pred), FVC 3.62 L (96% pred), FEV1/FVC 0.80; ΔFEV1 +0.05 L since last visit. ACT score 24 (well controlled). Technique checked: correct. Smoking: never.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Urology reply: PSA stable, prostate size modest. Advise continue current meds, repeat PSA in 6 months, consider surgery only if symptomatic progression.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Asthma, mild persistent. Patient reports occasional night cough twice weekly, uses salbutamol 3‑4 times/week. BPH: reports mild hesitancy, no incontinence. Exam: mild end‑expiratory wheeze, prostate slightly firm, no nodule. Spirometry: FEV1 2.70 L (88% pred), FVC 3.55 L (94% pred), FEV1/FVC 0.76; ΔFEV1 –0.20 L since last visit. ACT score 18 (not well controlled). Technique corrected: taught slow‑deep inhalation for dry powder inhaler. Smoking: never.
